steps.thought: List the available tests on the manufacturing test station to identify which test to run first.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power on selftest to check basic device enumeration across all major subsystems as the cheapest initial diagnostic step.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully with all CAN nodes, UART devices, camera sensor ID, and I2C devices correctly enumerated. This rules out immediate hardware enumeration failures across the power, communication, and camera subsystems.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on self test passed cleanly, though further subsystem tests are required before confirming a healthy unit.
Motor subsystem not yet tested under load.
Battery resting and load voltages not yet measured.
IMU static noise and bias logging not yet performed.

steps.thought: I will run the battery_rest_check to check pack and per-cell voltages at rest, as this is a cheap subsystem test to verify the battery condition before doing more expensive dynamic tests.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed cleanly with a pack voltage of 16.6V and a very low cell imbalance of 5mV, ruling out resting battery faults such as weak cells or high imbalance.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on and battery resting checks have both passed without any failures, though thorough testing of remaining subsystems is required.
Motors have not yet been spun up under load to check for bearing wear, vibration, or RPM jitter.
ESC telemetry and commutation stability remain unverified.
IMU static noise and sensor bias have not yet been logged via imu_static.
Compass static and motor interference tests have not yet been run.

steps.thought: Run esc_telemetry to check commutation and packet loss across all ESCs as the next logical subsystem check.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test failed due to high packet loss across all four ESCs (ranging from 7.61% to 9.39%), while back-EMF detection and temperatures are normal. This points toward a communication or bus-level issue affecting telemetry reporting from all ESCs.

hypotheses.rationale: High packet loss across all ESCs on the bus could be caused by improper CAN termination or signal reflection.
ESC telemetry shows minor sync errors on ESC 1 and ESC 2, requiring motor and ESC spin testing to verify.
Damaged harness wiring or stubs could cause general packet loss across multiple ESC nodes.
Unlikely given the widespread packet loss failures, but possible if the telemetry reporting itself is noisy.

steps.thought: I will run the harness_continuity test to check the CAN bus resistance and termination, which is the most direct and cheap way to investigate the widespread ESC telemetry packet loss.
steps.observation: The harness continuity test revealed a CAN termination resistance of 120.9 ohms, which is well outside the expected 54-66 ohm range, directly explaining the widespread packet loss observed across all ESC telemetry nodes.

hypotheses.rationale: CAN termination resistance reads 120.9 ohms instead of the terminated dual-resistor network expectation (around 60 ohms), which perfectly accounts for the severe packet loss on all ESC telemetry channels.
Less likely given the exact 120 ohm reading characteristic of a single terminator present or missing parallel termination rather than a stub resistance drop, but remains a harness defect possibility.

steps.thought: The CAN termination reading is 120.9 ohms, clearly indicating a missing CAN bus terminator, which explains the high packet loss across all ESC telemetry nodes. I will now propose the rework to install the missing CAN bus terminator.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
